title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (Analysis situs, 3rd version, 1986). F is a set of 'facettes' (pieces of a stratified or combinatorial space), ordered by a specialization relation X << F, and equipped with a symmetric disjointness relation F // G. M (strata) and L (minimal pieces, the 'lieux' or 'ouverts') are distinguished subsets.

Rapports. A 'rapport' (also called a semi-open set) is a subset closed under the double disjointness-orthogonal. The operators are cosmpr (orthogonal) and smpr / s-rap (closure). The rapports form a lattice Sigma deg_F, ordered by inclusion and equipped with an orthocomplement (the complement operation C_F). In modern terms, Sigma_F is the complete ortholattice of biorthogonally closed sets of the orthogonality space (F, //), i.e. the Galois-closed sets of the polarity given by //.

Condition Disj_Lambda (from p.65). Let Lambda be a subset of F, and set omb_Lambda(F) = {X in Lambda | X << F} (the 'shadow' of F in Lambda). The condition is: F // G if and only if every X in omb_Lambda(F) satisfies X // G. Under it, p.65 shows two things:
- cosmpr_F(A) = cosmpr_F(omb_Lambda A);
- if A is closed downward for <<, then omb_Lambda(A) = A ∩ Lambda.

Result on this page. Rapports are orthogonals, and by Disj they are downward closed. One therefore gets an order-preserving, complement-preserving bijection:
- Sigma deg_F -> Sigma deg_Lambda, A |-> A ∩ Lambda = omb_Lambda(A);
- Sigma deg_Lambda -> Sigma deg_F, S |-> s-rap_F(S) = {F in F | omb_Lambda(F) ⊂ S}.
In words: the ortholattice of rapports can be computed on any Lambda that is 'dense' in the sense of Disj.

Choice of Lambda. To 'understand' rapports one wants Lambda as small as possible. The natural choice is L, the minimal pieces, which is legitimate as soon as axiom AtL2 holds (described as a mild condition). Hence Sigma_F ≅ Sigma_M ≅ Sigma_L, each computed with the restricted relations //_F, //_M, //_L.

Best case. If //_L is the tautological relation x ≠ y (e.g. for a 'quasi-ensembliste' structure), then, as p.67 says, Sigma_L = P(L) and complementation is ordinary set complement. Supports become supp A = ouv(A) = ∪ ouv(F), and the distributivity 'perplexities' of pp.63–64 disappear because Sigma is then Boolean.

Purpose. This gives a combinatorial theory of supports and cosupports of subsets of a stratified object, with values in a 'lattice of open-like sets' that is canonically independent of the level (facets, strata, minimal pieces) at which it is computed.
errors: No real error. One gap: the page asserts without proof that S |-> {F | omb_Lambda(F) ⊂ S} lands in the F-rapports and inverts A |-> A∩Lambda. This needs S to be biorthogonally closed in (Lambda, //|Lambda) together with Disj_Lambda. It is routine, but some checking is left implicit.

The bijection is with ortholattices. In general Sigma need not be distributive; that is the source of the 'perplexities' of pp.63–64. Boolean structure is only guaranteed in special cases such as //_L being x ≠ y.
AtL2 is not stated on this page, so it cannot be checked here that AtL2 is exactly what makes L satisfy Disj_L.

ideas.what: Lattice of 'rapports': subsets closed under double orthogonality for a disjointness relation, with orthocomplement
ideas.modern_name: Ortholattice of biorthogonally closed sets of an orthogonality space (Birkhoff polarity / Galois connection); regular-open-type algebra
ideas.where_published: Only in these Analysis situs notes, as far as known

ideas.what: Restriction to a 'dense' subset Lambda satisfying Disj_Lambda gives an isomorphic lattice of rapports, via A |-> A∩Lambda and S |-> {F | omb(F) ⊂ S}
ideas.modern_name: Dense-subset invariance of the regular-open completion, RO(D) ≅ RO(P) for dense D ⊂ P (forcing); invariance of the orthogonality closure lattice under dense sub-orthogonality spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cohen/Scott/Solovay (forcing, 1960s); standard in Boolean-algebra completion theory

ideas.what: When //_L is x ≠ y, Sigma_L = P(L) with ordinary complement, so support = union of opens
ideas.modern_name: Atomic Boolean algebra / power set as orthogonality lattice of the discrete orthogonality

missed.claim: Grothendieck's reduction of the lattice of 'rapports' to the minimal pieces is structurally the forcing/Boolean-completion lemma that a dense subposet has the same regular-open algebra. It is set in a stratified-space context, where supports of sets of facets are valued in an ortholattice, with a criterion (here //_L being x ≠ y) for that lattice to be Boolean. The link between his 'analysis situs' supports and orthogonality spaces / regular-open completions is not made in the literature on his tame-topology program. It is a minor conceptual link, not a new theorem.
missed.quote: On trouve ainsi une correspondance bijective, entre les ens. de F-rapports et des Λ-rapports ... respectant les relations d'ordre (inclusion) et la relation de complémentaire
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This could frame his combinatorial stratified 'analysis situs' (posets of strata with a disjointness relation) using ortholattice / locale-theoretic tools. That may matter for combinatorial models of stratified spaces (exit-path posets, o-minimal cell decompositions).

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a clean but essentially routine lemma: closure lattices of an orthogonality relation are invariant under passage to a dense subset. It mirrors known results (forcing dense-subset lemma, orthogonality spaces). Its interest is mostly historical, as part of the unpublished 1986 combinatorial analysis situs.
transcription_corrections: Line 'ou moins qui est méchant' more plausibly reads '– ce n'est pas méchant' (meaning AtL2 is a mild requirement).
'(de façon un peu abus.)' probably reads '(abusivement, en laissant tomber les exposants ° de Σ ...)' — the dropped exponents are the ° in Σ°.
'(p.ex. cas y d'une structure quasi-ensembliste)': the stray 'y' is a pen mark; read '(p.ex. cas d'une structure quasi-ensembliste)'.
's-rap_F S' is correct (s-rapport generated by S). The 'F' subscript was overwritten in the manuscript.
The left-margin NB is largely illegible. It seems to say that the notion of rapport, defined via //_L, requires (AtL2), and that one may take L with the relation //_L; exact wording uncertain.
